name: Bajaj Consumer Care Ltd
title: Bajaj Consumer Care Ltd - 533229 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 gross margin hit 63% and EBITDA margin 25% standalone on MLH price cuts and mix, with management declining to guide and flagging hyperinflation in LLP and packaging from the Gulf war.

triggers.label: Gross margin 63% in Q4
triggers.quote: our gross margin stood at 63% for the quarter and 60% for the full year

triggers.label: No channel filling, distributor inventory lean
triggers.quote: At a distributor level also, our inventory is very lean and we are very happy with the status of our inventory at distributors.

triggers.label: Frontal pricing needed in Q1 on inflation
triggers.quote: in this quarter, I think we will have to take some amount of frontal pricing as well to manage the quarter

triggers.label: No formal guidance; margin band low-to-mid 20s
triggers.quote: we aspire to maintain margins between the low to the mid 20s

guidance.quote: we aspire to maintain margins between the low to the mid 20s
we will be further focusing on growing this portfolio to around INR500 crores in size over the next three years

red_flags.label: Input cost hyperinflation; price hikes needed
red_flags.quote: the war in the Gulf has created extreme volatility in the prices of LLP and packaging material

summary.headline: Bajaj Consumer Care Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to INR308 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% on MLH cuts and mix, but management guided no numbers.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue of INR308 crore (+28% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR327 crore (+32%), with standalone EBITDA of INR78 crore (25% margin, +131%) and consolidated PAT of INR63.6 crore (19.5% margin). Full-year net revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time at INR1,153 crore (+21%), with full-year EBITDA of INR224 crore (19.5%) and PAT of INR190 crore (16.5%). Margin gains were attributed to MLH (mix-linked holdings/pack-level) reductions held without revenue loss and favourable mix, while management flagged a hyperinflationary input-cost environment from the Gulf war and said pricing actions are being executed.

financial_highlights.change: Full year 60%, around 650 bps improvement YoY

segments.name: ADHO (core hair oil brand)
segments.commentary: Full-year revenue grew in the 20s percent; Q4 volume was near double-digit on an adjusted (MLH-adjusted) basis and mid-single digit on absolute basis. Advertising spend in Q4 rose 34% YoY.

segments.name: Non-ADHO growth portfolio
segments.commentary: Generated INR225 crore revenue in FY26, described as profitable; target is about INR500 crore in three years (roughly 30%+ CAGR), with Bajaj Coconut and Banjara's as key brands.

segments.name: Banjara's (acquired brand)
segments.commentary: In first year under Bajaj ownership, grew double digits with low-teen margin; sub-INR100 crore business. Vishal Personal Care (acquired Q1 FY26) and Banjara's together under 5% of revenue.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Declined in Q4 and for the year. Nepal grew with improving margin and Bangladesh reached breakeven; Rest of World and MENA are being repaired under new leadership.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; it reiterated an aspirational EBITDA margin range of low-to-mid 20s, and said it is confident of maintaining margins in the current approximate range.
Gross margin is expected to operate in the same zone over the medium term.
Management expects to take some front-end pricing in Q1 FY27 to manage input cost inflation; strategy to be frozen over the next month and fine-tuned in subsequent quarters.
Non-ADHO portfolio target of about INR500 crore in three years, excluding any future acquisitions which would be a top-up.
Advertising intensity described as the right level for the brand over the multi-year horizon; no FY27 A&SP forecast given.
capex_capacity: Project Aarohan (distribution expansion): phase 1 covered Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh; about two-thirds of business has gone through, remaining one-third (Bihar, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Odisha, etc.) to be covered in FY27.
Phase 3 of Aarohan begins in five new states, with work started at end of Q4 FY26.
Aarohan delivers roughly a 2-4% growth delta versus non-Aarohan areas, which management expects to sustain with lap-up risk as states mature.
demand_pricing: General trade grew high-teens for FY26; urban (direct retail and wholesale) grew about 20%, rural mid-teens. GT is about 70% of business, split equally urban and rural, with about half of urban being wholesale.
Organized trade grew in the 20s in Q4 and is now about 30% of sales; modern trade and e-commerce outperformed, while CSD/CPC was muted.
Management said there is no channel filling and distributor inventory is lean.

Input costs: mustard and copra prices have stayed at pre-war levels; LLP and packaging costs are volatile. Management said nearly 100% of the cost base is inflating, some at 50-60% and some at 20-30%.
Market share remains below 10% in the hair oil category, which management describes as a $2 billion+ market with 92% penetration.

qa_highlights.question: How did Q4 gross margin expand while COGS fell about 3% QoQ on ~6.7% sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a more accretive brand mix and volume roughly flat QoQ; it did not split brand-level data. Q4 gross margin was 63%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp EBITDA margin jump from ~18.5% in Q3 and how sustainable is it given cost inflation starting in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were MLH reductions supported by transaction growth without revenue loss, favourable mix, and revenue over-delivery. Management said the low-to-mid 20s range is unchanged and it is not worried about the coming quarter, but it is a dynamic situation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth picture and Aarohan contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: ADHO Q4 volume was near double-digit MLH-adjusted and mid-single digit absolute. Aarohan delivers about 2-4% growth delta versus non-Aarohan areas.

qa_highlights.question: Are there one-offs in Q4 and is the business sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the only inorganic factor is Vishal Personal Care, acquired in Q1 FY26, now in its first year of consolidation.

qa_highlights.question: Is any channel filling or GST-related destocking happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling and trade has not stocked up, with lean distributor inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will advertising intensity (~15% of revenue) fall in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast line-item costs given volatility, but said the current advertising level is the right level for the brand over the multi-year view and it intends to maintain it.

risks_watch: Input-cost inflation (LLP, packaging, mustard, copra) from the Gulf war; margin sustainability once current inventory cover runs out in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Price increases required in Q1 FY27 may affect volume; management said MLH-adjusted volume was near double-digit and absolute volume mid-single digit in Q4.
Lapping of high-growth bases from the revenue reset, with management expecting growth to taper after about two quarters.
International business decline and leadership change in Rest of World and MENA.
Aarohan benefit tapering as states lap up; remaining one-third of business yet to go through Aarohan.
Banjara's profitability depends on scale; it is kept as a separate unit, so cost integration is deferred.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and FY26 turnaround, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on forward margins and pricing, repeatedly declining to give guidance and citing input-cost volatility.
key_quotes: In this quarter, we registered a strong growth across all segments, channels and markets, building the confidence behind our brands and the strategy chosen by us.
We feel extremely confident in the place where we have reached with respect to our gross margins and intend to now operate in the same zone over a medium-term basis.
Naveen Pandey: Amit, let me clarify. We don't give guidances.
There is no channel filling for us, Shirish. There is just no channel filling for us.

growth.why: No formal numeric guidance; management reiterated an aspirational low-to-mid 20s EBITDA margin band and a non-ADHO portfolio target of about INR500 crore in three years (from INR225 crore), with Q1 FY27 pricing actions planned, but no capacity or order numbers back the growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 standalone EBITDA margin hit 25% (vs ~18.5% in Q3) on MLH cuts and mix, but management expects hyperinflationary input costs to hit from Q1-Q2 FY27, and it only aspires to hold the low-to-mid 20s band, so further expansion is unlikely.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (Aarohan phase 3 in five new states, work started end Q
rows.why: Project Aarohan distribution expansion is under way, with phase 3 started in five new states and the remaining one-third of business (Bihar, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Odisha etc.) to be covered in FY27, but this is distribution reach rather than plant capacity and no capacity numbers were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward, tapering after about two quarters
rows.why: Q4 ADHO volume was near double-digit MLH-adjusted and mid-single digit absolute, general trade grew high-teens in FY26, and Aarohan adds 2-4% growth delta, though Q1 FY27 pricing actions may dent volume and growth is expected to taper after two quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed on the call and no utilisation or capacity figures were given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric guidance and reiterated only an aspirational low-to-mid 20s EBITDA margin band, with cost inflation and Q1 FY27 pricing actions pending, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input costs are inflating across nearly 100% of the cost base (some at 50-60%, some at 20-30%) from the Gulf war, and management said current inventory cover runs out in Q1-Q2 FY27, which could compress the 25% standalone EBITDA margin.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Non-ADHO portfolio (INR225 crore in FY26) is targeted at about INR500 crore in three years via Bajaj Coconut and Banjara's, but no specific product launch dates were named.

rows.label: Front-end price increases in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management said it expects to take some front-end pricing in Q1 FY27 to manage input cost inflation, with strategy to be frozen over the next month, though the size is not disclosed.

rows.label: Aarohan phase 3 in five new states
rows.why: Phase 3 work began at end of Q4 FY26, and the remaining one-third of the business (Bihar, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Odisha etc.) is to be covered in FY27, delivering a 2-4% growth delta versus non-Aarohan areas.

rows.label: International business repair (Rest of World, MENA)
rows.why: International revenue declined in Q4 and for FY26, with Nepal growing and Bangladesh at breakeven, while Rest of World and MENA are being repaired under new leadership with no numbers given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q4 margin jump (standalone EBITDA 25%, gross margin 63%) and FY26 turnaround, but cautious and non-committal on forward margins and pricing, declining formal guidance amid hyperinflationary input costs; analysts probed margin sustainability once cost inflation starts
